title: Per-channel activation rescale profiles (INT8) — calibration pipeline, validation harness, and adaptive kernel selectors
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready per-channel activation rescale (SmoothQuant-style) workflow for INT8 serving. Deliver a calibration pipeline that emits stable per-layer activation scaling profiles, a lightweight profile manager in the runtime, accuracy-validation harness (automated regression checks), and adaptive kernel selection / fallback rules when quantized kernels fail or underperform.

Scope:
- Offline calibration harness to produce per-channel activation scales and weight quantization ranges. Supports per-layer and per-block modes.
- Profile format: compact JSON payload (versioned) that maps model scope -> tensor path -> {act_scale, weight_qparams, stats_ref}. Profiles must be human-readable and small (<= 200KB for LLM-7B).
- Calibration inputs: standardized prompt corpus (1000 sequences across token lengths), plus synthetic edge-case inputs for tails.
- Metrics recorded during calibration: token-level KL divergence, per-layer activation RMS, max/min histograms, and end-to-end perplexity on heldout sets.
- Validation harness: automated CI job that runs quantized model inference vs float baseline on small eval sets (SQuAD-style and LLM-next token) and emits pass/fail if top-1 token PPL delta > 0.5% or any identified layer shows KL > threshold.
- Runtime integration: profile manager that attaches profiles to model artifacts in the model registry, APIs to query active profile, and a small in-memory cache keyed by model-version+profile-hash.
- Kernel selection: adaptive selector that chooses (A) quantized fused kernel, (B) quantized non-fused kernel, or (C) float fallback kernel per operator at load-time based on profile flags and a safety checklist (profile confidence, hardware capabilities, recent mismatch counters).
- Fallback policy: optimistic enablement by default for new profiles but with runtime health checks (error rate, token divergence estimate derived from small sample) to automatically roll back to float kernels if degradation observed.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Calibration pipeline produces stable profiles with per-layer act_scale that reduce activation outliers compared to no-rescale.
2) Quantized inference with produced profile shows <0.5% PPL regression on our standard LLM validation split for 3 model families (7B, 13B, 70B) using representative sequence lengths.
3) Runtime can atomically attach/detach profiles and select kernels without restarting serving processes.
4) CI integration: every PR changing quantization code triggers validation harness and reports pass/fail.

Design notes / tradeoffs:
- We use per-channel act rescale because per-tensor rescale underestimates cross-channel variance for LLM attention heads; this increases profile size but improves accuracy.
- Profile format is intentionally simple JSON to keep inspection and small diffs easy; future iteration may compress to binary.
- We avoid tying this iteration to a single SmoothQuant reference implementation: calibration math follows the activation-rescale principle but we implement a conservative rescale multiplier clipping and per-layer confidence score to avoid aggressive rescaling that amplifies noise.
- Kernel selection is implemented as a policy table evaluated at model load; we keep the table small and append-only to minimize risk.

Artifacts / links:
- Prototype calibration repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-prototypes/pull/76
- Runtime profile manager stub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/engine/pull/3281
- Calibration corpus (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1q-Calibration-Corpus-2025
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12345678/Activation+Rescale+Profiles

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement pipeline + profile storage + validation harness. Run offline calibration for 7B and 13B.
- Phase 2: runtime rollout behind feature flag to small percentage of production traffic on dedicated capacity; monitor regression signals and token-level divergence metrics stored in Console.
- Phase 3: enable on-hosted API for low-latency models after 2-week stability.

Monitoring / telemetry:
- Add metrics: profile_apply_failure_count, kernel_mismatch_count, quant_fallback_rate, per_profile_ppl_delta_90p. Hook into Console dashboards and set regression alert at 1% PPL delta for customer-impacting deploys.

Longer-term: explore FP8 path for layers where INT8 quant is too lossy; profiles will carry flags for fp8_candidate:true/false.
